about: X3DH v2 vectors (design.md §3.1, §3.2, §3.6) generated by scripts/gen-vectors-v2.mjs from labelled secrets; every byte here was computed on both sides and the two sides agree. Draws are listed in order; feed them to a scripted-randomness provider in that order. Refusal vectors use ordinary randomness; each must fail with expected_code (null: any typed refusal) and leave every stored state and prekey unchanged.

kdf.cite: design.md:139 (§3.1 item 5) and design.md:200 (§3.5); X3DH rev 1 §2.2 (salt = HashLen zero bytes, 32 bytes of output)

parameters.dh_order: DH1 = DH(IK_A, SPK_B), DH2 = DH(EK_A, IK_B), DH3 = DH(EK_A, SPK_B), DH4 = DH(EK_A, OPK_B) only when a one-time prekey was served; KM = F || DH1 || DH2 || DH3 [|| DH4], 128 or 160 bytes
parameters.ad: 0x05 || IK_A (33), 0x05 || IK_B (33), 0xED || IKsig_A (33), 0xED || IKsig_B (33), dev_A (16 raw UUID bytes), dev_B (16); A is the initiator for the whole session
parameters.spk_signature: Ed25519 by IKsig over CBOR [domain, device_id (text string), IK (bstr 32), SPK (bstr 32), spk_id (uint)]
parameters.labels: secret(label) = SHA-256(UTF-8(prefix || label)); a draw of n <= 32 bytes is the first n bytes of secret(label); longer data is secret(label + "/0") || secret(label + "/1") || ... cut to length

refusals.name: swapped_sender_ik_sig_pub
refusals.what: session_init names another Ed25519 key (mallory's); the responder builds AD with it and the first message fails; no prekey is consumed

refusals.name: sk_without_f
refusals.what: a responder state built from SK derived without F (sk_without_f_hex) cannot read the first message

refusals.name: low_order_ek_zero
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: low_order_ek_one
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: low_order_ek_order_8_a
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: low_order_ek_order_8_b
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: low_order_ek_p_minus_1
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: low_order_ek_p
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: low_order_ek_p_plus_1
refusals.what: session_init carries a low-order EK; DH2 and DH3 are all zero and the bootstrap refuses

refusals.name: non_canonical_sender_device_id
refusals.what: session_init sender_device_id in uppercase

refusals.name: equal_device_ids
refusals.what: session_init sender and recipient are the same device, and the row names that device

refusals.name: sidecar_sender_differs_from_row
refusals.what: session_init names another sender device than the server row's sender_device_id
refusals.refusal: sidecar sender differs from the row

refusals.name: unknown_spk
refusals.what: session_init names a signed prekey id the responder does not hold

refusals.name: opk_id_without_used_opk
refusals.what: session_init has opk_id while used_opk is false

refusals.name: missing_sender_ik_sig_pub
refusals.what: session_init without sender_ik_sig_pub_b64

refusals.name: bundle_for_another_device
refusals.what: a correctly signed bundle that names another device than the one asked for (initiator side)

refusals.name: bundle_bad_signature
refusals.what: the bundle's SPK was replaced, so its signature fails (initiator side, before any pin or DH)

refusals.name: bundle_alg_unknown
refusals.what: a correctly signed bundle whose alg is "not-an-x3dh-alg", which is not the v2 X3DH alg string (initiator side, refused before the signature check)

refusals.name: bundle_alg_empty
refusals.what: a correctly signed bundle whose alg is "", which is not the v2 X3DH alg string (initiator side, refused before the signature check)

refusals.name: first_message_after_opk_deleted
refusals.what: the first message delivered again after the responder deleted the one-time prekey it used
